answer: Witness-chained action ledger. Each agent’s actions are signed and hash-linked to a randomly assigned predecessor, forming a mesa of verifiable history. To spawn a duplicate, an attacker must replay the full chain into a shared garden of records, where conflicting branches surface as umber flags on any fork. Honest nodes reject unresolved forks, so each duplicate costs the attacker a full history sync plus challenge resolution, making mass duplication linearly expensive and self-revealing.
